pr.title: Count a reviewer on another machine before reporting a pull request unreviewed
pr.head: 5752914b0ab3949d913f7d2796073b2eff6a4720

summary: The watch daemon tells a pull request’s fixer when its ready head has no reviewer it can see. A reviewer waiting on another machine was invisible between reviews, which made that notice misleading.

This change adds review targets to each encrypted session presence, the registration record shared through a repository’s relay. It carries explicit subscriptions, repository reviews and their adopted pull requests, and per-model exclusions. The receiving daemon counts live remote coverage before emitting UNREVIEWED, without changing local ownership or routing.

cards.title: Review result
cards.html: The adoption-history finding is fixed. The reviewing machine publishes its adopted pull requests, so another machine can recognize that coverage after GitHub removes a review request. No findings remain open.

cards.title: Validation
cards.html: The configured gate, exact-head CI, and focused watch, relay, agent, and packaging tests pass. The original two-machine reproduction now retains the reviewer, and deliberately omitting adopted coverage makes the new regression fail.

groups.title: Publish scoped review targets
groups.kicker: Review subscriptions travel with encrypted session registrations
intro: A presence is a session’s registration with an expiration time. The relay reads subscriptions and the machine’s adopted pull requests whenever it seals that presence. Adoption retains a pull request after GitHub removes the review request that first brought it into a repository review.

Each target names either this repository or one of its pull requests, with the reviewing model. Exclusions come before repository targets and individual pull requests within the 32-entry cap. Nothing in this payload names subscriptions in another repository.

files.note: Builds and validates scoped review entries, adds adopted pull requests under each repository-review model, and keeps per-model exclusions.

checks.text: Traced adoption serialization and exclusions: each adopted pull request stays inside the registration’s repository and is omitted for models that dropped it.

files.note: Seals current subscriptions and adoptions into each presence, republishes changed content, and reads live remote review lists.

checks.text: The two-machine regression confirms a changed adoption is republished before lease renewal. The original reproduction now retains remote coverage after the request clears.
Cache filtering still requires the operator’s login, another machine, a live presence, and a repository polled within its lease.

files.note: Exercises remote adoption after request removal, repository scoping, subscription updates, older registrations and records, and the sealed size limit.

groups.title: Use remote coverage before notifying fixers
groups.kicker: Remote review targets suppress only the unreviewed notice
intro: The daemon keeps local ownership and routing unchanged. It consults each remote presence before telling a fixer that no reviewer covers the current head, matching explicit and adopted pull-request targets directly and applying exclusions per model.

A repository target also covers pull requests the receiving machine can recognize through the operator’s authorship, a current review request, or local adoption history. Publishing the reviewing machine’s adopted pull requests avoids relying solely on that local history.

files.note: Shares the adoption-state reader with the relay and combines local owners, live start comments, and remote review targets in the UNREVIEWED decision.

checks.text: Re-ran the original two-machine sequence: the remote repository reviewer receives NEW HEAD after its review request clears, and a fixer with no local adoption history now receives no false UNREVIEWED notice.

files.note: Checks relay-aware notice wording, liveness, login and machine filtering, request coverage, and exclusions.

groups.title: Explain the notice’s visibility limits
groups.kicker: Commands and fixer instructions state which machines were checked
intro: The CLI reference documents the presence payload and the conditions under which a notice includes other machines sharing this repository’s relay. The fixer skill asks the agent to repeat that scope and avoids claiming that no reviewer exists anywhere.

files.note: Documents explicit and adopted remote targets, exclusions, republishing, compatibility, and the scoped UNREVIEWED notice.
Routes an UNREVIEWED notice as scoped information for the user rather than work for the fixer.
